source.text: הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־הָיָ֤ה אֶֽל־יִרְמְיָ֨הוּ֙ מֵאֵ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה בַּשָּׁנָה֙ הָעֲשִׂרִ֔ית לְצִדְקִיָּ֖הוּ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה הִ֧יא הַשָּׁנָ֛ה שְׁמֹנֶֽה־עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה לִנְבֽוּכַדְרֶאצַּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: The word that came to Jeremiah from with Yahweh in the year the tenth of Zedekiah king of Judah; it [was] the year eight-teen year of Nebuchadrezzar.

en.L: The word that came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the tenth year of Zedekiah king of Judah; that [was] the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar.
en.B: This message came to Jeremiah from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in the tenth year of Zedekiah's reign over Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar's reign.
en.R: This is the message {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Jeremiah in Zedekiah's tenth year as king of Judah. It was Nebuchadrezzar's eighteenth year as king of Babylon.

es.L: La palabra que vino a Jeremías de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} en el año décimo de Sedequías, rey de Judá; ese [era] el año dieciocho de Nabucodorosor.
es.B: Este mensaje vino a Jeremías de parte {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} en el décimo año del reinado de Sedequías sobre Judá, que era el año dieciocho del reinado de Nabucodorosor.
es.R: Este es el mensaje que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} le dio a Jeremías en el décimo año del reinado de Sedequías sobre Judá. Era el año dieciocho del reinado de Nabucodorosor en Babilonia.

fr.L: La parole qui fut adressée à Jérémie de la part {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} la dixième année de Sédécias, roi de Juda ; c’[était] la dix-huitième année de Nabuchodonosor.
fr.B: Ce message fut adressé à Jérémie par {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} la dixième année du règne de Sédécias sur Juda, qui était la dix-huitième année du règne de Nabuchodonosor.
fr.R: Voici le message que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a donné à Jérémie la dixième année où Sédécias était roi de Juda. C’était la dix-huitième année où Nabuchodonosor était roi de Babylone.

sw.L: Neno lililomjia Yeremia kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} katika mwaka wa kumi wa Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda; huo [ulikuwa] mwaka wa kumi na nane wa Nebukadreza.
sw.B: Ujumbe huu ulimjia Yeremia kutoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} katika mwaka wa kumi wa utawala wa Sedekia juu ya Yuda, ambao ulikuwa mwaka wa kumi na nane wa utawala wa Nebukadreza.
sw.R: Huu ndio ujumbe ambao {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alimpa Yeremia katika mwaka wa kumi wa Sedekia kama mfalme wa Yuda. Ulikuwa mwaka wa kumi na nane wa Nebukadreza kama mfalme wa Babeli.

vi.L: Lời từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với Giê-rê-mi vào năm thứ mười đời Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa; ấy [là] năm thứ mười tám đời Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa.
vi.B: Sứ điệp này từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đến với Giê-rê-mi vào năm thứ mười triều Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa, cũng là năm thứ mười tám triều Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa.
vi.R: Đây là sứ điệp {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} ban cho Giê-rê-mi vào năm thứ mười Sê-đê-kia làm vua Giu-đa. Đó là năm thứ mười tám Nê-bu-cát-rết-sa làm vua Ba-by-lôn.

decisions.choice: the tenth year of Zedekiah, the eighteenth of Nebuchadrezzar: 588-587 BC, during the siege of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The verse dates the word by both kings. Zedekiah began to reign in 597 BC, so his tenth year was 588-587 BC. Nebuchadrezzar became king of Babylon in 605 BC, the fourth year of Jehoiakim (25:1), so this was his eighteenth year by the same reckoning. The siege had begun in Zedekiah's ninth year (39:1; 52:4), and the city fell a year later, in his eleventh year and Nebuchadrezzar's nineteenth (52:5, 12; 2 Kings 25:2, 8). Jeremiah 52:29 counts the same eighteenth year for a group of captives taken from Jerusalem. So the word came while the city was surrounded and its end was near.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadrezzar: the form of the name with r, as the Hebrew has it here
decisions.reason: Jeremiah mostly spells the Babylonian king's name Nebuchadrezzar, close to its Babylonian form; chapters 27-29 and the books of Kings use Nebuchadnezzar. Both name the same king (see 21:2; 25:1).

decisions.choice: in the year: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has "in the year of" and the margin tells readers to read "in the year". The meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: the heading of the chapter: the word itself begins in verse 6
decisions.reason: Verses 2-5 describe the situation in which the word came: the siege, and why Jeremiah was a prisoner. The word of the LORD is told from verse 6, in Jeremiah's own voice.

decisions.choice: The word that came to Jeremiah from the LORD (L); This message came to Jeremiah from the LORD (B); This is the message the LORD gave Jeremiah (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this heading throughout Jeremiah. Readable says how the years are counted and adds "king of Babylon" so that the foreign king is clear.

source.text: וְאָ֗ז חֵ֚יל מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל צָרִ֖ים עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְיִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֗יא הָיָ֤ה כָלוּא֙ בַּחֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בֵּֽית־מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And then [the] army of [the] king of Babylon [were] besieging against Jerusalem; and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in [the] courtyard of the guard which [was in the] house of [the] king of Judah,

en.L: And then the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem, and Jeremiah the prophet was shut up in the courtyard of the guard, which [was in] the house of the king of Judah,
en.B: The army of the king of Babylon was then laying siege to Jerusalem, and the prophet Jeremiah was being held in the courtyard of the guard at the palace of the king of Judah,
en.R: At that time the army of the king of Babylon had surrounded Jerusalem to attack it. The prophet Jeremiah was locked up in the courtyard of the guard, an open court in the palace of the king of Judah.

es.L: Y entonces el ejército del rey de Babilonia sitiaba a Jerusalén, y el profeta Jeremías estaba encerrado en el patio de la guardia, que [estaba en] la casa del rey de Judá,
es.B: El ejército del rey de Babilonia tenía entonces sitiada a Jerusalén, y el profeta Jeremías estaba detenido en el patio de la guardia, en el palacio del rey de Judá,
es.R: En ese tiempo el ejército del rey de Babilonia había rodeado Jerusalén para atacarla. El profeta Jeremías estaba encerrado en el patio de la guardia, un patio abierto dentro del palacio del rey de Judá.

fr.L: Et alors l’armée du roi de Babylone assiégeait Jérusalem, et Jérémie le prophète était enfermé dans la cour de la garde, qui [était dans] la maison du roi de Juda,
fr.B: L’armée du roi de Babylone assiégeait alors Jérusalem, et le prophète Jérémie était détenu dans la cour de la garde, au palais du roi de Juda,
fr.R: À ce moment-là, l’armée du roi de Babylone encerclait Jérusalem pour l’attaquer. Le prophète Jérémie était enfermé dans la cour de la garde, une cour à ciel ouvert dans le palais du roi de Juda.

sw.L: Na wakati huo jeshi la mfalme wa Babeli lilikuwa likiuzingira Yerusalemu, na Yeremia nabii alikuwa amefungwa katika ua wa walinzi, uliokuwa [katika] nyumba ya mfalme wa Yuda,
sw.B: Wakati huo jeshi la mfalme wa Babeli lilikuwa limeuzingira Yerusalemu, na nabii Yeremia alikuwa amezuiliwa katika ua wa walinzi kwenye jumba la mfalme wa Yuda,
sw.R: Wakati huo jeshi la mfalme wa Babeli lilikuwa limeuzunguka Yerusalemu ili kuushambulia. Nabii Yeremia alikuwa amefungiwa katika ua wa walinzi, uwanja ulio wazi katika jumba la mfalme wa Yuda.

vi.L: Bấy giờ đạo quân của vua Ba-by-lôn đang vây hãm Giê-ru-sa-lem, và tiên tri Giê-rê-mi bị giam trong sân lính canh, [ở trong] cung vua Giu-đa,
vi.B: Lúc ấy đạo quân của vua Ba-by-lôn đang vây hãm Giê-ru-sa-lem, còn tiên tri Giê-rê-mi đang bị giam trong sân lính canh thuộc cung vua Giu-đa,
vi.R: Lúc ấy quân đội của vua Ba-by-lôn đã bao vây Giê-ru-sa-lem để tấn công. Tiên tri Giê-rê-mi đang bị nhốt trong sân lính canh, là một cái sân trong cung vua Giu-đa.

decisions.choice: the courtyard of the guard: a guarded court within the royal palace, used to hold prisoners
decisions.reason: The courtyard was part of the palace complex south of the temple (Nehemiah 3:25). A prisoner held there was confined but could receive visitors and speak with people, as this chapter shows (verses 8 and 12). Jeremiah had been moved there from a dungeon at his own plea to Zedekiah (37:15-21), and he stayed there until the city fell (38:28).

decisions.choice: the army of the king of Babylon was besieging Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The siege began in Zedekiah's ninth year (39:1). For a time the Babylonians drew back when an Egyptian army came up, and it was then that Jeremiah was arrested (37:5, 11-16). By now the siege had been renewed.

decisions.choice: which was in the house of the king: the courtyard lay within the palace
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "which [was] the house of the king"; the courtyard belonged to the palace grounds. The sentence runs on into verse 3, which says why Jeremiah was there.

decisions.choice: courtyard of the guard (all levels); palace (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Courtyard of the guard" is kept as in Nehemiah 3:25. Readable adds that it was an open court in the palace. Balanced and Readable say "palace" for the king's house, and Literal and Balanced end with a comma because the sentence continues.

decisions.choice: el patio de la guardia
decisions.reason: The guarded court of the palace (meaning decision m1) is "el patio de la guardia" at every level through the chapters that name it.

decisions.choice: ua wa walinzi
decisions.reason: "The courtyard of the guard" is a guarded open court, not a prison cell, so every level says "ua wa walinzi", as the English keeps "courtyard of the guard".

decisions.choice: "la cour de la garde" at every level
decisions.reason: The guarded court within the palace (meaning decision m1), named the same way through Jeremiah 32-39.

decisions.choice: "sân lính canh" (courtyard of the guard) at every level
decisions.reason: One name for the guarded court where Jeremiah is held, used through chapters 32-33 (and 37-39); it was a court, not a prison cell.

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֣ר כְּלָא֔וֹ צִדְקִיָּ֥הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר מַדּוּעַ֩ אַתָּ֨ה נִבָּ֜א לֵאמֹ֗ר כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הִנְנִ֨י נֹתֵ֜ן אֶת־הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את בְּיַ֥ד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל וּלְכָדָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: where shut him up Zedekiah king of Judah, saying, Why you [are] prophesying, saying, Thus says Yahweh: Look I [am] giving the city this into [the] hand of [the] king of Babylon, and he will capture it;

en.L: where Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up, saying, "Why do you prophesy, saying, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am giving this city into the hand of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it;
en.B: for Zedekiah king of Judah had confined him there. He had said, "Why do you prophesy as you do? You say, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am about to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.
en.R: King Zedekiah of Judah had locked him up there. Zedekiah had asked him, "Why do you keep prophesying these things? You say, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to hand this city over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it.

es.L: donde lo había encerrado Sedequías, rey de Judá, diciendo: «¿Por qué profetizas, diciendo: “Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: He aquí, yo entrego esta ciudad en mano del rey de Babilonia, y él la tomará;
es.B: porque Sedequías, rey de Judá, lo había encerrado allí. Le había dicho: «¿Por qué profetizas así? Tú dices: “{{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} dice esto: Voy a entregar esta ciudad en manos del rey de Babilonia, y él la tomará.
es.R: El rey Sedequías de Judá lo había encerrado allí. Sedequías le había preguntado: «¿Por qué sigues profetizando estas cosas? Tú dices: “Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: Voy a entregar esta ciudad al rey de Babilonia, y él la tomará.

fr.B: car Sédécias, roi de Juda, l’y avait fait enfermer. Il lui avait dit : « Pourquoi prophétises-tu ainsi ? Tu dis : “{{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit ceci : Je vais livrer cette ville au roi de Babylone, et il la prendra.
fr.R: Le roi Sédécias de Juda l’avait fait enfermer là. Sédécias lui avait demandé : « Pourquoi continues-tu à annoncer ces choses ? Tu dis : “Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} : Je vais livrer cette ville au roi de Babylone, et il la prendra.

sw.L: ambapo Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda alikuwa amemfunga, akisema, "Kwa nini unatabiri, ukisema, '{{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asema hivi: Tazama, ninautia mji huu mkononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli, naye atautwaa;
sw.B: kwa maana Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda alikuwa amemfungia huko. Alikuwa amesema, "Kwa nini unatabiri hivyo? Unasema, 'Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} asemavyo: Ninakaribia kuutia mji huu mikononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli, naye atauteka.
sw.R: Mfalme Sedekia wa Yuda alikuwa amemfungia huko. Sedekia alikuwa amemuuliza, "Kwa nini unaendelea kutabiri mambo haya? Unasema, 'Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} analosema: Nitautia mji huu mikononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli, naye atauteka.

vi.L: nơi Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa đã giam ông mà nói rằng: "Sao ngươi nói tiên tri rằng: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán thế này: Kìa, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ phó thành này vào tay vua Ba-by-lôn, và vua ấy sẽ chiếm lấy nó;
vi.B: vì Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa đã giam ông ở đó. Vua đã nói: "Sao ngươi lại nói tiên tri như vậy? Ngươi nói: '{{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán như vầy: Ta sắp phó thành này vào tay vua Ba-by-lôn, và vua ấy sẽ chiếm lấy nó.
vi.R: Vua Sê-đê-kia của Giu-đa đã nhốt ông ở đó. Sê-đê-kia đã hỏi ông: "Sao ngươi cứ nói tiên tri những điều như thế? Ngươi nói: 'Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: Ta sắp phó thành này vào tay vua Ba-by-lôn, và vua ấy sẽ chiếm lấy nó.

decisions.choice: Zedekiah's question, quoting Jeremiah's own message back to him, runs to the end of verse 5
decisions.reason: The king had imprisoned Jeremiah for what he preached. His complaint repeats the prophet's words: the city will fall, the king will be taken to Babylon, and fighting is useless. The same message is given in 21:4-7, 34:2-5 and 37:17.

decisions.choice: prophesy: speak as a prophet, declaring a message as the LORD's word
decisions.reason: The king does not deny that Jeremiah speaks in the LORD's name; he resents what the message says and the harm he thinks it does to the city's defense (38:4).

decisions.choice: as you do? You say (B); keep prophesying these things? You say (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "saying" introduces the words Jeremiah keeps repeating. Balanced and Readable close the question first and then give the message as what Jeremiah says, so that the long quotation does not end in a question.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (L); The LORD says this (B); This is what the LORD says (R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula in Isaiah and Jeremiah. Inside Zedekiah's speech the prophet's words take single quotation marks.

decisions.choice: the king says "ngươi" to Jeremiah here
decisions.reason: Zedekiah speaks in anger to a prisoner, so he uses "ngươi"; the terms note's "ông" is kept for his private consultations with Jeremiah (37-38).

source.text: וְצִדְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֔ה לֹ֥א יִמָּלֵ֖ט מִיַּ֣ד הַכַּשְׂדִּ֑ים כִּ֣י הִנָּתֹ֤ן יִנָּתֵן֙ בְּיַ֣ד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֔ל וְדִבֶּר־פִּ֣יו עִם־פִּ֔יו וְעֵינָ֖יו אֶת־עֵינָ֥יו תִּרְאֶֽינָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Zedekiah king of Judah not will escape from [the] hand of the Chaldeans; for surely he will be given into [the] hand of [the] king of Babylon, and will speak his mouth with his mouth, and his eyes his eyes will see;

en.L: and Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the hand of the Chaldeans, for he will surely be given into the hand of the king of Babylon, and his mouth will speak with his mouth, and his eyes will see his eyes;
en.B: Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the Chaldeans. He will certainly be handed over to the king of Babylon; he will speak with him face to face and see him with his own eyes.
en.R: Zedekiah king of Judah will not escape from the Babylonians. He will surely be handed over to the king of Babylon. He will have to stand before that king and speak with him face to face, and see him with his own eyes.

es.L: y Sedequías, rey de Judá, no escapará de la mano de los caldeos, sino que de cierto será entregado en mano del rey de Babilonia, y su boca hablará con la boca de él, y sus ojos verán los ojos de él;
es.B: Sedequías, rey de Judá, no escapará de los caldeos. De seguro será entregado al rey de Babilonia; hablará con él cara a cara y lo verá con sus propios ojos.
es.R: Sedequías, rey de Judá, no escapará de los babilonios. De seguro será entregado al rey de Babilonia. Tendrá que presentarse ante ese rey y hablar con él cara a cara, y lo verá con sus propios ojos.

fr.L: et Sédécias, roi de Juda, n’échappera pas à la main des Chaldéens, car il sera certainement livré entre les mains du roi de Babylone, et sa bouche parlera avec sa bouche, et ses yeux verront ses yeux ;
fr.B: Sédécias, roi de Juda, n’échappera pas aux Chaldéens. Il sera certainement livré au roi de Babylone ; il lui parlera face à face et le verra de ses propres yeux.
fr.R: Sédécias, roi de Juda, n’échappera pas aux Babyloniens. Il sera sûrement livré au roi de Babylone. Il devra se présenter devant ce roi et lui parler face à face, et il le verra de ses propres yeux.

sw.L: na Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda hataokoka mkononi mwa Wakaldayo, kwa maana hakika atatiwa mkononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli, na kinywa chake kitasema na kinywa chake, na macho yake yataona macho yake;
sw.B: Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda hataokoka mikononi mwa Wakaldayo. Hakika atatiwa mikononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli; atasema naye ana kwa ana na kumwona kwa macho yake mwenyewe.
sw.R: Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda hataokoka mikononi mwa Wababeli. Hakika atatiwa mikononi mwa mfalme wa Babeli. Atalazimika kusimama mbele ya mfalme huyo na kusema naye ana kwa ana, na kumwona kwa macho yake mwenyewe.

vi.L: Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa sẽ không thoát khỏi tay người Canh-đê, vì chắc chắn nó sẽ bị phó vào tay vua Ba-by-lôn, miệng nó sẽ nói với miệng vua ấy, và mắt nó sẽ thấy mắt vua ấy;
vi.B: Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa sẽ không thoát khỏi tay người Canh-đê. Chắc chắn nó sẽ bị phó vào tay vua Ba-by-lôn; nó sẽ nói chuyện mặt đối mặt và tận mắt thấy vua ấy.
vi.R: Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa sẽ không thoát khỏi tay quân Ba-by-lôn. Chắc chắn nó sẽ bị giao cho vua Ba-by-lôn. Nó sẽ phải đứng trước mặt vua ấy, nói chuyện mặt đối mặt và tận mắt thấy vua ấy.

decisions.choice: his mouth will speak with his mouth, and his eyes will see his eyes: Zedekiah will meet the king of Babylon in person
decisions.reason: The first "his" in each pair is Zedekiah, the second the king of Babylon. The picture is of a face-to-face meeting with the conqueror, as a captive before his judge. The same words are in 34:3, and it happened at Riblah (39:5-7; 52:9-11).

decisions.choice: he will surely be given: the verb is doubled for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the verb, "being given he will be given": there is no doubt about it.

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans were the people of southern Mesopotamia whose dynasty ruled Babylon at this time; in Jeremiah the name means the Babylonian army and nation (21:4).

decisions.choice: speak with him face to face and see him with his own eyes (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of the paired "mouth" and "eyes" sayings and make clear who is meant; Literal keeps the Hebrew picture. Readable says "Babylonians" for "Chaldeans", as in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: until I visit him: until God deals with him, in a sense left open
alternatives: until I take care of him
decisions.reason: The verb means to attend to someone, and it can be used of punishing or of caring for. Here it may mean until his death, or until God's judgment on him is complete. Jeremiah 34:4-5 promises Zedekiah that he will not die by the sword but in peace, with mourning, while 52:11 says he was kept in prison in Babylon until the day he died. The open phrase allows either thought.

decisions.choice: though you fight ... you will not succeed: resistance is useless
decisions.reason: The word that begins the clause can mean "if", "when" or "though". Jeremiah's message was that the city should surrender to Babylon to live (21:9; 38:17-18), and this is what Zedekiah held against him.

decisions.choice: the end of Zedekiah's question begun in verse 3
decisions.reason: The question "Why do you prophesy ...?" covers all of Jeremiah's words that he quotes, so the quotation closes here.

decisions.choice: visit (L); deal with (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use "deal with", which keeps the openness of the Hebrew between punishment and care.

decisions.choice: The king of Babylon (R); Zedekiah (B)
decisions.reason: Readable names the subject of "will take", and Balanced names Zedekiah as the one who will stay, so that the two "he"s are not confused.

decisions.choice: "je m'occupe de lui" (B, R); "je le visite" (L)
decisions.reason: French "s'occuper de" keeps open whether God will punish or care for him, as the English "deal with" does (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: "thăm viếng" (visit)
decisions.reason: Meaning decision m1 leaves open whether God's "visit" here is for good or ill, so Literal keeps the neutral "thăm viếng" rather than a word that settles it.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah said: his own account of the purchase and his prayer follow, to verse 25
decisions.reason: After the setting in verses 1-5, Jeremiah tells in the first person how the word came, how he bought the field (verses 7-15) and how he prayed (verses 16-25). From verse 26 the narrator speaks of him again by name, and the LORD's answer runs to verse 44.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD came to me, saying (L); came to me (B); The LORD gave me this message (R); no quotation marks for Jeremiah's account
decisions.reason: The wording set for this formula throughout Jeremiah. Jeremiah's first-person account is set as narrative, without quotation marks, as in 13:1-11 and 24:1-10; the words of the LORD and of others within it take quotation marks.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah's own account (verses 6-25) without quotation marks, in the first-person narrative tenses (passé simple at L and B, passé composé at R)

decisions.choice: the right of redemption: the duty and right of the nearest relative to buy family land so it is not lost to the family
decisions.reason: The Law said that when an Israelite became poor and had to sell land, his nearest relative, his redeemer (go'el), should come and buy back what was sold (Leviticus 25:25). Land was the family's lasting share in the land the LORD had given, and it was meant to stay in the family (Leviticus 25:23-24; Numbers 27:8-11). Ruth 4:1-10 shows a redeemer buying a field in the same way. Hanamel offers Jeremiah, as next in line, the first right to buy.

decisions.choice: Hanamel son of Shallum your uncle: Jeremiah's first cousin
decisions.reason: The word means a father's brother, an uncle. Shallum was the brother of Jeremiah's father Hilkiah (1:1), so his son Hanamel was Jeremiah's cousin. This Shallum is not King Shallum of 22:11; the name was common.

decisions.choice: Anathoth: Jeremiah's home town
decisions.reason: Anathoth was a town of priests in the land of Benjamin, a few miles north of Jerusalem (1:1; Joshua 21:18). Its men had once plotted to kill Jeremiah (11:21-23). The land around it was now held by the Babylonian army.

decisions.choice: look: God tells Jeremiah in advance what will happen
decisions.reason: The LORD announces the visit before it comes, so that when Hanamel arrives Jeremiah will know the offer is from the LORD (verse 8).

decisions.choice: redemption (L); family redeemer (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the noun "redemption". Balanced and Readable name the one who holds the right, the "family redeemer", as in Ruth 2:20, so that readers see that it is a family duty and not a religious term.

decisions.choice: Your cousin (R); and keep it in the family (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the relationship and says what redeeming the field was for.

decisions.choice: el derecho de rescate (Literal); pariente redentor (Balanced); el pariente que debe rescatar la tierra (Readable)
decisions.reason: The right of the nearest relative to buy family land (meaning decision m1); Balanced uses "redentor", the word the terms note sets for *goʾel*, and Readable explains it.

decisions.choice: Hanamel
decisions.reason: The name follows the Hebrew form, as the data's English does.

decisions.choice: baba mdogo
decisions.reason: Hebrew *dod* is the father's brother. Swahili "mjomba" properly means the mother's brother, so every level says "baba (yako/yangu) mdogo", as the published 1 Samuel 10:14 ("baba mdogo wa Sauli") and 2 Kings 24:17 ("baba mdogo wa Yehoyakini"); 32:8, 9 and 12 L follow. Readable and Basic call Hanameli "binamu" (cousin) where the English does.

decisions.choice: haki ya ukombozi (Literal); mkombozi wa jamaa (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The kinsman's right to buy back family land (Leviticus 25:25), with "kukomboa" as the terms note sets for redeeming.

decisions.choice: "Hanaméel fils de Shalloum"; "le droit de rachat" (L, B), "le proche parent qui a le droit de racheter" (R)
decisions.reason: The usual French form of the name; the right of the go'el is named with "racheter", the verb the terms note sets for this root, as in Ruth.

decisions.choice: "quyền chuộc" (L); "người có quyền chuộc sản nghiệp" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The redemption of family land (go'el), worded with "chuộc", the verb used for God's redeeming in 31:11, so the reader hears the same idea. The cousins say "anh" and "tôi" to each other.

source.text: וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵ֠לַי חֲנַמְאֵ֨ל בֶּן־דֹּדִ֜י כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ אֶל־חֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָה֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֡י קְנֵ֣ה נָ֠א אֶת־שָׂדִ֨י אֲשֶׁר־בַּעֲנָת֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֣ר׀בְּאֶ֣רֶץ בִּנְיָמִ֗ין כִּֽי־לְךָ֞ מִשְׁפַּ֧ט הַיְרֻשָּׁ֛ה וּלְךָ֥ הַגְּאֻלָּ֖ה קְנֵה־לָ֑ךְ וָאֵדַ֕ע כִּ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And came to me Hanamel son of my uncle according to [the] word of Yahweh to [the] courtyard of the guard, and he said to me, Buy please my field which [is] in Anathoth which [is] in [the] land of Benjamin, for to you [belongs the] right of the possession, and to you the redemption; buy for yourself. And I knew that [the] word of Yahweh it [was].

en.L: And Hanamel the son of my uncle came to me, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to the courtyard of the guard, and he said to me, "Buy, please, my field that [is] at Anathoth, which [is] in the land of Benjamin, for the right of possession [is] yours, and the redemption [is] yours; buy [it] for yourself." And I knew that this [was] the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Then my cousin Hanamel visited me in the courtyard of the guard, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said. He told me, "Please buy my field at Anathoth in the territory of Benjamin. The right of inheritance is yours, and so is the right of redemption; buy it for yourself." I knew then that this was the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: Then my cousin Hanamel came to see me in the courtyard of the guard, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told me he would. He said, "Please buy my field at Anathoth in the land of Benjamin. You have the right to inherit it, and you have the right to buy it back for the family. Buy it for yourself." Then I knew that this message had come from {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Y vino a mí Hanamel, el hijo de mi tío, conforme a la palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, al patio de la guardia, y me dijo: «Compra, te ruego, mi campo que [está] en Anatot, que [está] en la tierra de Benjamín, porque tuyo [es] el derecho de posesión, y tuyo el rescate; cómpra[lo] para ti». Y supe que era palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Entonces mi primo Hanamel vino a verme al patio de la guardia, tal como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} había dicho. Me dijo: «Por favor, compra mi campo de Anatot, en el territorio de Benjamín. Tuyo es el derecho de herencia, y tuyo también el derecho de rescate; cómpralo para ti». Entonces supe que esto era palabra {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.R: Entonces mi primo Hanamel vino a verme al patio de la guardia, como {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} me había dicho que haría. Me dijo: «Por favor, compra mi campo de Anatot, en la tierra de Benjamín. Tú tienes el derecho de heredarlo, y tienes el derecho de comprarlo para la familia. Cómpralo para ti». Entonces supe que ese mensaje había venido {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Et Hanaméel, le fils de mon oncle, vint vers moi, selon la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, dans la cour de la garde, et il me dit : « Achète donc mon champ qui [est] à Anatoth, dans le pays de Benjamin, car le droit d’héritage est à toi, et le rachat est à toi ; achète-[le] pour toi. » Et je sus que c’[était] la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Alors mon cousin Hanaméel vint me trouver dans la cour de la garde, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} l’avait dit. Il me dit : « Achète donc mon champ d’Anatoth, dans le territoire de Benjamin. Le droit d’héritage est à toi, et le droit de rachat aussi ; achète-le pour toi. » Je compris alors que c’était la parole {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Alors mon cousin Hanaméel est venu me voir dans la cour de la garde, comme {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} me l’avait annoncé. Il m’a dit : « S’il te plaît, achète mon champ d’Anatoth, dans le pays de Benjamin. Tu as le droit d’en hériter, et tu as le droit de le racheter pour la famille. Achète-le pour toi. » Alors j’ai su que ce message venait {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Basi Hanameli mwana wa baba yangu mdogo akanijia, sawasawa na neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, katika ua wa walinzi, akaniambia, "Tafadhali nunua shamba langu lililo Anathothi, lililo katika nchi ya Benyamini, kwa maana haki ya urithi [ni] yako, na ukombozi [ni] wako; jinunulie." Ndipo nikajua kwamba hilo [lilikuwa] neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Kisha binamu yangu Hanameli alinijia katika ua wa walinzi, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa amesema. Akaniambia, "Tafadhali nunua shamba langu lililoko Anathothi katika nchi ya Benyamini. Haki ya urithi ni yako, na haki ya ukombozi pia; jinunulie." Ndipo nikajua kwamba hilo lilikuwa neno la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Kisha binamu yangu Hanameli alikuja kuniona katika ua wa walinzi, kama {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alivyokuwa ameniambia kwamba angekuja. Akasema, "Tafadhali nunua shamba langu lililoko Anathothi katika nchi ya Benyamini. Una haki ya kulirithi, na una haki ya kulinunua ili libaki katika jamaa. Jinunulie." Ndipo nikajua kwamba ujumbe ule ulikuwa umetoka kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Ha-na-mên con trai chú tôi đến với tôi trong sân lính canh, đúng như lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, và nói với tôi: "Xin anh hãy mua cánh đồng của tôi ở A-na-tốt, thuộc đất Bên-gia-min, vì quyền thừa hưởng [là] của anh, và quyền chuộc [là] của anh; hãy mua cho mình." Bấy giờ tôi biết rằng đó [là] lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Rồi Ha-na-mên, anh em họ của tôi, đến thăm tôi trong sân lính canh, đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán. Anh ấy nói với tôi: "Xin anh mua cánh đồng của tôi ở A-na-tốt, trong địa phận Bên-gia-min. Quyền thừa hưởng là của anh, quyền chuộc cũng là của anh; anh hãy mua lấy." Bấy giờ tôi biết đó là lời của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Rồi Ha-na-mên, anh em họ của tôi, đến gặp tôi trong sân lính canh, đúng như {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã báo trước. Anh ấy nói: "Xin anh mua cánh đồng của tôi ở A-na-tốt trong đất Bên-gia-min. Anh có quyền thừa hưởng nó, và anh có quyền chuộc nó lại cho gia đình. Anh hãy mua lấy." Bấy giờ tôi biết sứ điệp ấy đã đến từ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.

decisions.choice: the right of possession: the right to hold the land as an inheritance
decisions.reason: The word means a possession held by inheritance. As the next heir, Jeremiah had the right to own the family land, and the right of redemption gave him the duty to buy it so that it did not pass outside the family (verse 7).

decisions.choice: and I knew that this was the word of the LORD: the event confirmed the word
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had heard the LORD's word in verse 7; when Hanamel came and spoke exactly as he had been told, he knew that the command to buy came from the LORD. The purchase is a sign, explained in verse 15.

decisions.choice: in the land of Benjamin: the tribal territory north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Anathoth lay in Benjamin's territory. Jeremiah had tried to go there during a pause in the siege to settle a share of property among his people, and was arrested as a deserter (37:12-14).

decisions.choice: please: a polite request
decisions.reason: The small word softens the request. Hanamel asks rather than demands; perhaps he needed the money, perhaps he wished to be rid of land in enemy hands.

decisions.choice: my cousin (B, R); just as the LORD had said (B); as the LORD had told me he would (R)
decisions.reason: "The son of my uncle" is a cousin. "According to the word of the LORD" means that it happened as the LORD said it would, and Balanced and Readable put it that way.

source.text: וָֽאֶקְנֶה֙ אֶת־הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה מֵאֵ֛ת חֲנַמְאֵ֥ל בֶּן־דֹּדִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּעֲנָת֑וֹת וָֽאֶשְׁקֲלָה־לּוֹ֙ אֶת־הַכֶּ֔סֶף שִׁבְעָ֥ה שְׁקָלִ֖ים וַעֲשָׂרָ֥ה הַכָּֽסֶף׃

records.literal_gloss: And I bought the field from with Hanamel son of my uncle which [was] in Anathoth, and I weighed out to him the silver, seven shekels and ten the silver.

en.L: And I bought the field from Hanamel the son of my uncle, which [was] at Anathoth, and I weighed out the silver for him, seventeen shekels of silver.
en.B: So I bought the field at Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel, and I weighed out the price for him: {{units:about 7 ounces of silver|seventeen shekels of silver}}.
en.R: So I bought the field at Anathoth from my cousin Hanamel. I weighed out the price for him, {{units:about 7 ounces of silver|seventeen shekels of silver}}.

es.L: Y compré el campo de Hanamel, el hijo de mi tío, que [estaba] en Anatot, y le pesé la plata, diecisiete siclos de plata.
es.B: Así que le compré a mi primo Hanamel el campo de Anatot, y le pesé el precio: {{units:unos 200 gramos de plata|diecisiete siclos de plata}}.
es.R: Así que le compré a mi primo Hanamel el campo de Anatot. Le pesé el precio, {{units:unos 200 gramos de plata|diecisiete siclos de plata}}.

fr.L: Et j’achetai le champ de Hanaméel, le fils de mon oncle, qui [était] à Anatoth, et je lui pesai l’argent, dix-sept sicles d’argent.
fr.B: J’achetai donc à mon cousin Hanaméel le champ d’Anatoth, et je lui pesai le prix : {{units:environ 200 grammes d’argent|dix-sept sicles d’argent}}.
fr.R: J’ai donc acheté à mon cousin Hanaméel le champ d’Anatoth. Je lui ai pesé le prix, {{units:environ 200 grammes d’argent|dix-sept sicles d’argent}}.

sw.L: Nami nikalinunua shamba lile lililo Anathothi kutoka kwa Hanameli mwana wa baba yangu mdogo, nikampimia fedha, shekeli kumi na saba za fedha.
sw.B: Basi nililinunua shamba lililoko Anathothi kutoka kwa binamu yangu Hanameli, nikampimia bei yake: {{units:karibu gramu 200 za fedha|shekeli kumi na saba za fedha}}.
sw.R: Basi nililinunua shamba lililoko Anathothi kutoka kwa binamu yangu Hanameli. Nikampimia bei yake, {{units:karibu gramu 200 za fedha|shekeli kumi na saba za fedha}}.

vi.L: Tôi mua cánh đồng ở A-na-tốt của Ha-na-mên con trai chú tôi, và tôi cân bạc cho anh ấy, mười bảy siếc-lơ bạc.
vi.B: Vậy tôi mua cánh đồng ở A-na-tốt của Ha-na-mên, anh em họ của tôi, và cân tiền trả cho anh ấy: {{units:khoảng 200 gam bạc|mười bảy siếc-lơ bạc}}.
vi.R: Vậy tôi mua cánh đồng ở A-na-tốt của Ha-na-mên, anh em họ của tôi. Tôi cân tiền trả cho anh ấy, {{units:khoảng 200 gam bạc|mười bảy siếc-lơ bạc}}.

decisions.choice: I weighed out the silver: payment by weight, before coins were used
decisions.reason: Money in Judah was silver weighed on scales (verse 10; Genesis 23:16). The shekel was a weight, about two-fifths of an ounce, not a coin. Seventeen shekels is a modest sum, but the size of the field is not given, and land near a besieged city in enemy hands could not have fetched much.

decisions.choice: seven shekels and ten: seventeen
decisions.reason: Hebrew can put the units before the tens; "seven shekels and ten" is seventeen shekels.

decisions.choice: about 7 ounces of silver (B, R; original unit as the alternative)
decisions.reason: Seventeen shekels at about two-fifths of an ounce each is about 7 ounces. Literal keeps the Hebrew unit; Balanced and Readable give the modern measure with the shekel as the setting's alternative.

decisions.choice: the price (B, R)
decisions.reason: The first "silver" in the verse is the payment; Balanced and Readable say "price" so that "silver" is not said twice.

decisions.choice: {{units:unos 200 gramos de plata|diecisiete siclos de plata}}
decisions.reason: Seventeen shekels at 11.5 g each, rounded as the English rounds ("about 7 ounces"); the original unit is the alternative, and Literal keeps "siclos".

decisions.choice: karibu gramu 200 za fedha
alternatives: shekeli kumi na saba za fedha
decisions.reason: Swahili gives metric weight by default with the shekels as the alternative, as the Swahili style sets (the English converts to ounces); Literal keeps the shekels.

decisions.choice: "environ 200 grammes d'argent", with "dix-sept sicles d'argent" as the units alternative
decisions.reason: French takes the metric measure by default, as the style guide sets: seventeen shekels at about 11.5 g each come to about 200 g. Literal keeps the Hebrew unit.

decisions.choice: "khoảng 200 gam bạc", with "mười bảy siếc-lơ bạc" as the units alternative
decisions.reason: Vietnamese settings give metric by default and the original unit as the alternative (style guide, section 7), unlike the English US units; seventeen shekels of about 11.5 g each is close to 200 g. Literal keeps the shekels.

source.text: וָאֶכְתֹּ֤ב בַּסֵּ֨פֶר֙ וָֽאֶחְתֹּ֔ם וָאָעֵ֖ד עֵדִ֑ים וָאֶשְׁקֹ֥ל הַכֶּ֖סֶף בְּמֹאזְנָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And I wrote in the deed and I sealed, and I caused to witness witnesses, and I weighed out the silver on scales.

en.L: And I wrote in the deed and sealed [it], and I had witnesses attest [it], and I weighed out the silver on the scales.
en.B: I signed the deed and sealed it, had it witnessed, and weighed the silver on scales.
en.R: I signed the deed and sealed it, and I had witnesses sign it too. Then I weighed out the silver on a scale.

es.L: Y escribí en la escritura y [la] sellé, e hice que testigos [la] certificaran, y pesé la plata en la balanza.
es.B: Firmé la escritura y la sellé, la hice certificar por testigos y pesé la plata en la balanza.
es.R: Firmé la escritura y la sellé, e hice que unos testigos también la firmaran. Después pesé la plata en una balanza.

fr.L: Et j’écrivis dans l’acte et je [le] scellai, et je [le] fis attester par des témoins, et je pesai l’argent sur la balance.
fr.B: Je signai l’acte et le scellai, je le fis attester par des témoins et je pesai l’argent sur une balance.
fr.R: J’ai signé l’acte et je l’ai scellé, et j’ai fait signer des témoins. Puis j’ai pesé l’argent sur une balance.

sw.L: Nikaandika katika hati na kuitia muhuri, nikawashuhudisha mashahidi, nikaipima fedha katika mizani.
sw.B: Niliiandika hati na kuitia muhuri, nikawaweka mashahidi waishuhudie, nikaipima fedha katika mizani.
sw.R: Niliiandika hati na kuitia muhuri, nikawaambia mashahidi waitie sahihi pia. Kisha nikaipima fedha katika mizani.

vi.L: Tôi viết vào khế ước và đóng ấn, rồi mời các nhân chứng làm chứng, và tôi cân bạc trên cân.
vi.B: Tôi ký khế ước, đóng ấn, nhờ nhân chứng làm chứng, rồi cân bạc trên cân.
vi.R: Tôi ký vào khế ước và đóng ấn, rồi nhờ các nhân chứng cùng ký tên. Sau đó tôi cân bạc trên cân.

decisions.choice: I wrote in the deed: signed it, putting his name to it
decisions.reason: The verb is "wrote", with "in the deed". The witnesses "wrote in the deed" too (verse 12), which shows that signing is meant: each party put his name or mark on the document. The deed itself may have been drawn up by a scribe.

decisions.choice: sealed it and had witnesses: the legal steps of a land sale
decisions.reason: A contract for land was written, sealed and witnessed, and the payment weighed in front of the witnesses, so that the sale could be proved later (verse 44). Sealing meant rolling or folding the document and closing it with clay or wax pressed with a seal.

decisions.choice: had witnesses attest it (L); had it witnessed (B); had witnesses sign it (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "I caused witnesses to witness" repeats one root. Each level says what the witnesses did in its own way; Readable says "sign" because verse 12 says they wrote on the deed.

decisions.choice: "khế ước" (deed)
decisions.reason: "Khế ước" is the established word for a written contract of sale, used for the deed through verses 10-16 and 44.

source.text: וָאֶקַּ֖ח אֶת־סֵ֣פֶר הַמִּקְנָ֑ה אֶת־הֶֽחָת֛וּם הַמִּצְוָ֥ה וְהַחֻקִּ֖ים וְאֶת־הַגָּלֽוּי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I took the deed of the purchase, the sealed [one], the terms and the conditions, and the open [one].

en.L: And I took the deed of the purchase, the sealed [copy], the terms and the conditions, and the open [copy].
en.B: Then I took the deed of purchase, both the sealed copy, containing the terms and conditions, and the open copy.
en.R: Then I took the two copies of the deed of purchase. One copy, which had the terms and conditions of the sale, was sealed. The other copy was left open.

es.L: Y tomé la escritura de la compra, la [copia] sellada, con los términos y las condiciones, y la [copia] abierta.
es.B: Luego tomé la escritura de compra, tanto la copia sellada, que contenía los términos y las condiciones, como la copia abierta.
es.R: Luego tomé las dos copias de la escritura de compra. Una copia, que tenía los términos y las condiciones de la venta, estaba sellada. La otra copia quedó abierta.

fr.L: Et je pris l’acte d’achat, celui qui était scellé, les termes et les conditions, et celui qui était ouvert.
fr.B: Puis je pris l’acte d’achat, l’exemplaire scellé, qui contenait les termes et les conditions, et l’exemplaire ouvert.
fr.R: Puis j’ai pris les deux exemplaires de l’acte d’achat. Un exemplaire, qui contenait les termes et les conditions de la vente, était scellé. L’autre exemplaire était resté ouvert.

sw.L: Nikaichukua hati ya ununuzi, ile iliyotiwa muhuri, yenye masharti na kanuni, na ile iliyo wazi.
sw.B: Kisha nikaichukua hati ya ununuzi, nakala iliyotiwa muhuri, yenye masharti na kanuni, pamoja na nakala iliyo wazi.
sw.R: Kisha nikazichukua nakala mbili za hati ya ununuzi. Nakala moja, iliyokuwa na masharti na kanuni za mauzo, ilitiwa muhuri. Nakala nyingine iliachwa wazi.

vi.L: Rồi tôi lấy khế ước mua bán, bản đã đóng ấn, [có] các điều khoản và điều kiện, cùng bản để mở.
vi.B: Rồi tôi lấy khế ước mua bán, cả bản đã đóng ấn có ghi các điều khoản và điều kiện, lẫn bản để mở.
vi.R: Rồi tôi lấy hai bản khế ước mua bán. Một bản ghi các điều khoản và điều kiện của việc mua bán thì được đóng ấn. Bản kia được để mở.

decisions.choice: the sealed copy and the open copy: a deed written twice
decisions.reason: Documents of the time were often written twice, sometimes on one sheet. One copy was rolled up and sealed so that no one could change it; the other was left open so that it could be read without breaking the seals. If the open copy was ever disputed, the sealed one could be opened in front of witnesses. Verse 14 calls them two deeds.

decisions.choice: the terms and the conditions: what the sealed copy contained
alternatives: the sealed copy, sealed according to the law and its rules
decisions.reason: The two words stand between "the sealed one" and "the open one". They are taken as saying what the sealed copy held: the full details of the sale. They might instead describe the deed as a whole, or the legal formulas by which it was sealed.

decisions.choice: terms and conditions: the words for command and statute used of a contract
decisions.reason: The two words are the usual ones for a commandment and a statute in the Law. Here they are used of the legal terms of a business document.

decisions.choice: copy (all levels); two copies (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the sealed" and "the open"; English needs a noun, bracketed at Literal. Readable says there were two copies.

source.text: וָאֶתֵּ֞ן אֶת־הַסֵּ֣פֶר הַמִּקְנָ֗ה אֶל־בָּר֣וּךְ בֶּן־נֵרִיָּה֮ בֶּן־מַחְסֵיָה֒ לְעֵינֵי֙ חֲנַמְאֵ֣ל דֹּדִ֔י וּלְעֵינֵי֙ הָֽעֵדִ֔ים הַכֹּתְבִ֖ים בְּסֵ֣פֶר הַמִּקְנָ֑ה לְעֵינֵי֙ כָּל־הַיְּהוּדִ֔ים הַיֹּשְׁבִ֖ים בַּחֲצַ֥ר הַמַּטָּרָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And I gave the deed of the purchase to Baruch son of Neriah son of Mahseiah to [the] eyes of Hanamel my uncle and to [the] eyes of the witnesses, the [ones] writing in [the] deed of the purchase, to [the] eyes of all the Judeans, the [ones] sitting in [the] courtyard of the guard.

en.L: And I gave the deed of the purchase to Baruch son of Neriah son of Mahseiah before the eyes of Hanamel [son of] my uncle, and before the eyes of the witnesses who wrote in the deed of the purchase, before the eyes of all the Judeans who were sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
en.B: I gave the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, while my cousin Hanamel looked on, along with the witnesses who had signed the deed and all the Judeans who were sitting in the courtyard of the guard.
en.R: I gave the deed to Baruch son of Neriah and grandson of Mahseiah. My cousin Hanamel saw me do it. So did the witnesses who had signed the deed, and all the men of Judah who were sitting in the courtyard of the guard.

es.L: Y di la escritura de la compra a Baruc hijo de Nerías, hijo de Mahseías, ante los ojos de Hanamel, [el hijo de] mi tío, y ante los ojos de los testigos que escribieron en la escritura de la compra, ante los ojos de todos los judíos que estaban sentados en el patio de la guardia.
es.B: Le di la escritura de compra a Baruc hijo de Nerías, hijo de Mahseías, en presencia de mi primo Hanamel y de los testigos que habían firmado la escritura, y de todos los judíos que estaban sentados en el patio de la guardia.
es.R: Le di la escritura a Baruc, hijo de Nerías y nieto de Mahseías. Mi primo Hanamel me vio hacerlo. También lo vieron los testigos que habían firmado la escritura, y todos los hombres de Judá que estaban sentados en el patio de la guardia.

fr.L: Et je remis l’acte d’achat à Baruch fils de Nériya, fils de Mahséya, sous les yeux de Hanaméel, [le fils de] mon oncle, et sous les yeux des témoins qui avaient écrit dans l’acte d’achat, sous les yeux de tous les Judéens qui étaient assis dans la cour de la garde.
fr.B: Je remis l’acte d’achat à Baruch fils de Nériya, fils de Mahséya, sous les yeux de mon cousin Hanaméel, des témoins qui avaient signé l’acte, et de tous les Judéens qui étaient assis dans la cour de la garde.
fr.R: J’ai donné l’acte à Baruch, fils de Nériya et petit-fils de Mahséya. Mon cousin Hanaméel m’a vu le faire. Les témoins qui avaient signé l’acte l’ont vu aussi, ainsi que tous les hommes de Juda qui étaient assis dans la cour de la garde.

sw.L: Nikampa Baruku mwana wa Neria mwana wa Mahseya hati ya ununuzi mbele ya macho ya Hanameli [mwana wa] baba yangu mdogo, na mbele ya macho ya mashahidi walioandika katika hati ya ununuzi, mbele ya macho ya Wayahudi wote waliokuwa wameketi katika ua wa walinzi.
sw.B: Nilimpa Baruku mwana wa Neria, mwana wa Mahseya, hati ya ununuzi, binamu yangu Hanameli akitazama, pamoja na mashahidi waliokuwa wameitia sahihi hati hiyo na Wayahudi wote waliokuwa wameketi katika ua wa walinzi.
sw.R: Nilimpa Baruku mwana wa Neria na mjukuu wa Mahseya hati hiyo. Binamu yangu Hanameli aliniona nikifanya hivyo. Vivyo hivyo mashahidi waliokuwa wameitia sahihi hati hiyo, na watu wote wa Yuda waliokuwa wameketi katika ua wa walinzi.

vi.L: Tôi trao khế ước mua bán cho Ba-rúc con trai Nê-ri-gia, con trai Mạc-sê-gia, trước mắt Ha-na-mên [con trai] chú tôi, trước mắt các nhân chứng đã ký tên vào khế ước mua bán, và trước mắt mọi người Giu-đa đang ngồi trong sân lính canh.
vi.B: Tôi trao khế ước mua bán cho Ba-rúc con trai Nê-ri-gia, cháu Mạc-sê-gia, trước mặt Ha-na-mên, anh em họ của tôi, cùng các nhân chứng đã ký tên vào khế ước và mọi người Giu-đa đang ngồi trong sân lính canh.
vi.R: Tôi trao khế ước cho Ba-rúc, con trai Nê-ri-gia, cháu Mạc-sê-gia. Ha-na-mên, anh em họ của tôi, thấy tôi làm điều đó. Các nhân chứng đã ký tên vào khế ước và mọi người Giu-đa đang ngồi trong sân lính canh cũng thấy.

decisions.choice: Baruch son of Neriah: Jeremiah's scribe and companion
decisions.reason: Baruch is named here for the first time in the book's order. He wrote down Jeremiah's words and read them in the temple (36:4-10, 32), went with him into Egypt (43:6) and received a word of his own (45:1-5). A scribe was the right person to keep legal documents.

decisions.choice: Hanamel my uncle: read as "the son of my uncle", as in verses 8 and 9
alternatives: Hanamel my uncle, as the Hebrew stands
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here says "Hanamel my uncle", but Hanamel is the son of Jeremiah's uncle Shallum (verses 7-9). The word "son of" may have dropped out in copying, or the phrase may be a short way of naming the family relationship. Some Hebrew manuscripts and the ancient Greek translation read "the son of my uncle".

decisions.choice: before the eyes of: in the sight of, as witnesses
decisions.reason: The phrase comes three times: the sale was public, done in front of the seller, the signing witnesses and all who were present, so that no one could later deny it.

decisions.choice: the Judeans: the people of Judah present in the courtyard
decisions.reason: The word names people of Judah; here those who were in the courtyard of the guard, perhaps guards, other prisoners or visitors.

decisions.choice: [son of] my uncle (L); my cousin (B, R)
decisions.reason: Following m2, Literal brackets the words "son of" and Balanced and Readable say "cousin". Readable says "grandson of Mahseiah" for the second "son of", and "men of Judah" for those sitting in the courtyard.

decisions.choice: Baruc hijo de Nerías, hijo de Mahseías
decisions.reason: The form the terms note sets ("Baruc hijo de Nerías"); "Mahseías" keeps the Hebrew name apart from "Maasías" (Maaseiah).

decisions.choice: Baruku mwana wa Neria
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili form of Baruch's name; Mahseiah as "Mahseya".

decisions.choice: "Baruch fils de Nériya"
decisions.reason: The French form the terms note sets for Jeremiah's scribe.

decisions.choice: "Ba-rúc con trai Nê-ri-gia"; "Mạc-sê-gia"
decisions.reason: The terms note's form for Baruch son of Neriah, new in Vietnamese (Luke 3:27's "Nê-ri" is another name); "Mạc-sê-gia" is new too.

source.text: וָֽאֲצַוֶּה֙ אֶתבָּר֔וּךְ לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I charged Baruch to their eyes, saying:

decisions.choice: an earthenware vessel: a clay jar for keeping documents
decisions.reason: Clay jars were used to store scrolls and documents, since they kept out damp and pests; the scrolls found near the Dead Sea had been kept in jars for some two thousand years. Sealed in a jar, the deeds would survive the fall of the city and the long exile.

decisions.choice: take: the verb form gives a firm command
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the plain infinitive of the verb, which can serve as a strong order.

decisions.choice: so that they may last many days: be preserved for a long time
decisions.reason: The deeds are to be kept until the time when land is bought and sold again (verse 15). Jeremiah later says the exile will last seventy years (25:11; 29:10).

decisions.choice: the LORD of hosts (L); the LORD of Armies (B, R)
decisions.reason: The wording set for this title in Isaiah and Jeremiah; the main note is at Isaiah 1:9. Jeremiah's words to Baruch open a quotation that closes at the end of verse 15.

decisions.choice: deeds (L); documents (B); two copies (R)
decisions.reason: The plural names the two copies of verse 11. Balanced says "documents" and Readable "two copies" so that the list reads plainly.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah says "hãy" to Baruch with no pronoun
decisions.reason: The words are God's command passed on to Baruch, so Vietnamese gives them as a plain command; Jeremiah's relation to his scribe needs no pronoun here.
